description_good_justification: The README describes NVIDIA GPU sharing with Volcano, GPU memory and compute limits, and supported deployment requirements: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README explains how to obtain and install the software and links to GitHub issues and the contributing guide: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/README.md#contributing-and-security
contribution_justification: The contributing guide explains issue discussion, topic branches, pull requests, tests and DCO sign-offs: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#submitting-changes
contribution_requirements_justification: Contributions require maintainer review, resolved conversations, passing checks, tests for behavior changes and signed-off commits. The linked HAMi guide gives coding and formatting expectations: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#review-requirements
floss_license_justification: The project is released under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is an OSI-approved license: https://opensource.org/license/apache-2-0
license_location_justification: The repository root contains the Apache-2.0 LICENSE file: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers prerequisites, installation, scheduler configuration, Pod resource requests and metrics: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: Configuration inputs are documented in doc/config.md; the README documents Pod resource inputs, advertised node resources and the metrics endpoint. The device plugin executable provides generated --help for its CLI options: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/doc/config.md ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/README.md ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/cmd/vgpu/main.go
sites_https_justification: The project website, public source repository and image download site support HTTPS: https://project-hami.io ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin ; https://hub.docker.com/r/projecthami/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin
discussion_justification: GitHub issues provide searchable, URL-addressable discussions and permit participation through a web browser: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues
english_justification: The README and contribution guide are in English; English bug reports and review discussions are accepted in the issue tracker: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/README.md ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues
maintained_justification: The repository has recent merged changes, maintainer reviews and working CI, including the November 2026 v1.13.0 tag: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/commits/main/ ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
repo_public_justification: The Git source repository is publicly readable: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin
repo_track_justification: Git commits record changes, authors and dates: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/commits/main/
repo_interim_justification: Development commits and pull request revisions are published between releases: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/pulls
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses Git, a distributed version control system: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin
version_unique_justification: Plugin releases have distinct version identifiers and source tags, such as v1.12.0 and v1.13.0: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/tags
version_semver_justification: Plugin release identifiers use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example v1.13.0. The historical v1.9 tag aliases v1.9.0 at the same commit: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
version_tags_justification: Source releases are identified with Git tags: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md provides human-readable summaries for all existing plugin release tags and explains the historical v1.9 alias. The v1.11.0, v1.12.0, v1.13.0 and chart release also have published GitHub release notes: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/releases
report_process_justification: Users can submit bug reports through GitHub issues; a bug-report template requests the problem, expected behavior, reproduction steps and environment: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/new/choose ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.md
report_responses_justification: For requests opened from 2025-11-21 through 2026-11-21, a review of 34 bug reports found human acknowledgements on 19, more than half. Bot responses and reporter-only follow-ups were excluded. Examples: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/97 ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/134 ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/143
enhancement_responses_justification: For requests opened from 2025-11-21 through 2026-11-21, a review of 21 enhancement and maintenance requests found human replies, accepted linked changes or human review on 20. Bot responses and requester-only follow-ups were excluded. Examples: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/129 ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/155 ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues/193
report_archive_justification: The public issue tracker retains reports and responses, including closed issues: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md explains supported versions, private vulnerability reporting and a target initial response within five working days: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Security reports are accepted privately through GitHub Security Advisories rather than public issues: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
build_justification: Makefile and docker/Dockerfile automate building the Go executables and pinned HAMi-core library into the image. CONTRIBUTING.md documents source builds. A recent main image build completed successfully: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/Makefile ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/docker/Dockerfile ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/actions/runs/44703613581
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses common tools including Go, GNU Make, Docker Buildx and CMake: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/Makefile ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/docker/Dockerfile
build_floss_tools_justification: The documented complete image build compiles HAMi-core's CUDA test targets with NVIDIA's proprietary CUDA compiler via CMake find_package(CUDA) and cuda_add_executable. The Go component uses FLOSS Go and GCC; the complete documented image build still requires the NVIDIA toolchain: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/docker/Dockerfile ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/HAMi-core/blob/3d2f7f107bbce4dd422c9b2d3d37d439cfdfd21c/test/CMakeLists.txt
test_justification: The Apache-2.0 repository contains automated Go tests. CONTRIBUTING.md and CI document running them with go test ./...: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-tests ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unit-test.yaml
test_invocation_justification: The standard Go test invocation is documented: go test ./...: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-tests
test_most_justification: Coverage of most code branches and functionality has not been demonstrated. A fresh Go 1.27.3 run on the 2026-11-21 main revision measured 27.9% statement coverage with go test -race -count=1 -coverprofile=coverage.out ./... followed by go tool cover -func=coverage.out. Statement coverage is not branch coverage; native HAMi-core code is outside that Go measurement: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/tree/02dc12520cae24f3834c7438a9527abe7bf108d8
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Unit Test workflow runs on pull requests and pushes to main: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unit-test.yaml
test_policy_justification: Behavior changes require new or updated tests that fail without the change, and obsolete tests must be fixed or removed with the change: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major allocation and health changes include regression tests, including the changes released in v1.13.0: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/pull/223 ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/pull/216
tests_documented_added_justification: The contribution guide documents the requirement for tests alongside behavior changes: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-tests
warnings_justification: CI runs go vet and golangci-lint to detect code quality errors and common mistakes in Go code: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unit-test.yaml
warnings_fixed_justification: The configured Go vet and golangci-lint checks pass, as demonstrated by recent CI. Review requirements mandate passing build checks: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/actions/runs/44703613482 ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#review-requirements
warnings_strict_justification: Go vet and the default golangci-lint configuration are enabled, and HAMi-core uses -Wall. A maximally strict warning profile across all shipped code has not been established: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unit-test.yaml ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/HAMi-core/blob/3d2f7f107bbce4dd422c9b2d3d37d439cfdfd21c/CMakeLists.txt
crypto_published_justification: The plugin uses Kubernetes client-go for API-server TLS, which delegates to Go crypto/tls. Client-go requires TLS 1.2 or later; default TLS protocols and algorithms are publicly specified and reviewed: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/pkg/util/client/client.go ; https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/transport/transport.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/defaults.go
crypto_call_justification: The project delegates Kubernetes connection cryptography to client-go and Go's cryptographic libraries rather than implementing cryptographic primitives: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/pkg/util/client/client.go ; https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/transport/transport.go
crypto_floss_justification: Kubernetes client-go is Apache-2.0 and Go's TLS and cryptographic implementation is BSD-licensed; the API-client cryptographic functionality can run on FLOSS Linux: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/LICENSE ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/LICENSE ; https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/transport/transport.go
crypto_working_justification: Client-go defaults to TLS 1.2 or later with Go's default cipher selection. Go 1.27.3 excludes RC4, 3DES and static RSA key exchange from its default cipher suites. The application does not replace the TLS cryptographic implementation: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/transport/transport.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go
crypto_pfs_justification: Kubernetes client TLS uses Go's default cipher and key exchange selection. Default TLS 1.2 suites use ephemeral ECDHE, and TLS 1.3 uses ephemeral key exchanges; static RSA key exchange is disabled by default: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/transport/transport.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/defaults.go
crypto_password_storage_justification: The device plugin and monitor do not authenticate external users with a stored password database. Kubernetes credentials are used for outbound API authentication: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/pkg/util/client/client.go
crypto_random_justification: The client-go TLS configuration leaves Rand unset. Go crypto/tls therefore uses crypto/rand.Reader for TLS random values and ephemeral key generation: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.37.2/transport/transport.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/common.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/handshake_client.go ; https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/crypto/tls/key_agreement.go
delivery_mitm_justification: Source and release downloads use GitHub HTTPS and images are distributed by HTTPS registries. SECURITY.md also documents cosign identity verification for signed release images: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/releases ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-release-images
delivery_unsigned_justification: The Docker build retrieves the Go archive over HTTPS and checks its pinned SHA-256 digest. The release workflow obtains image digests through the registry and signs by digest; no HTTP-fetched unsigned checksum is used by these delivery paths: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/docker/Dockerfile ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-image-build.yml
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL analyzes Go code and GitHub Actions on pull requests, pushes to main and weekly. It was added before v1.13.0 and runs in the normal change workflow: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/pull/162
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's standard Go security queries cover common vulnerability classes: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml ; https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/go/
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push to main and each pull request revision, with an additional weekly scan: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Go regression tests use many assertions from testing and testify; these test assertions run during go test and are excluded from production binaries. The published fuzz targets also check decoder invariants: https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/pkg/plugin/health_test.go ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/pkg/util/fuzz_test.go ; https://github.com/Project-HAMi/volcano-vgpu-device-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/unit-test.yaml
